title: Democratic Republic of Vietnam

endonym.native: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa

capsule: The Republic of Vietnam (Việt Nam Cộng hòa), commonly called South Vietnam, was a non-communist state in the southern half of Vietnam, proclaimed on 26 October 1955 after Ngô Đình Diệm deposed Bảo Đại; the country had been provisionally partitioned at the 17th parallel by the 1954 Geneva Accords. Diệm ruled until his assassination in a US-backed coup on 2 November 1963, after which a period of governmental instability gave way to the presidency of Nguyễn Văn Thiệu from 1967. Dependent on American military and economic aid, the Republic fought the Viet Cong and the North Vietnamese Army; after the 1973 Paris Peace Accords and the US withdrawal, a Northern offensive captured Saigon on 30 April 1975, and the state was absorbed into the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on 2 July 1976.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Republic of Vietnam's territory is well-defined by the 1954 Geneva partition at the 17th parallel, with contested control of rural areas documented in U.S. military hamlet surveys and CORDS reports.
